prompt:
A desktop landing page for sqwer, a free touch-typing course for beginners and schools, rendered edge to edge as a finished website screen with crisp readable text, no browser window, no device, no desk.

The visitor has never touch-typed and needs to be guided from the first lesson. The page is built as the definitive touch-typing course book, reissued for today: deep ultramarine book cloth as the page ground at the top, opening onto a printed lesson plate on clean blue-white paper. Fine ruled drill lines, a precise colour-banded finger-zone chart of a keyboard, small printed captions, plate numbers.

What leads: the open lesson plate across the first viewport. On the left page, set in an elegant high-contrast serif: "Lesson 1. F and J." and the title "Learn to type properly, one key at a time." with a short line "12 chapters, 125 short lessons, free." On the right page, the full keyboard drawn as a finger-zone chart, each finger's keys in its own band of colour (violet, teal, coral, sky blue, rose), F and J marked with their small bumps, labelled "Plate 1. Where each finger rests". A single ultramarine button set like a bookmark ribbon: "Get started". Below, a contents page begins: "Part one Letters, Part two Capitals, marks and numbers, Part three Words and flow, Part four Speed and mastery".

Frame: the sqwer wordmark top left, navigation "Learn  Practice  Ranked" in small caps, "Sign in" at the far right. Clean grotesk for labels, monospace for drill lines like "fff jjj fjf jfj".
note: Free-plan output carries an OpenArt watermark; small text is garbled by the model.
